question: Let $P(X)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients of degree $d>0$. (a) If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are two integers such that $P(\alpha)=1$ and $P(\beta)=-1$, then prove that $|\beta-\alpha|$ divides 2. (b) Prove that the number of distinct integer roots of $P^2(x)-1$ is at most $d+2$.

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
